title: All-organic mixed-matrix membranes with single-crystal covalent organic frameworks for carbon capture - Nature Energy
gist: Chinese-led Nature Energy paper reports all-organic mixed-matrix membranes embedding single-crystal covalent organic frameworks at up to 75.5 vol% loading, reaching CO2 permeability of 74,800 Barrer at CO2/N2 selectivity of about 20 and retaining about 85% of permeability after six months of ageing. Only the abstract is available in the text.

insights.claim: All-organic mixed-matrix membranes embedding single-crystal covalent organic frameworks achieve CO2 permeability of 74,800 Barrer while keeping CO2/N2 selectivity of about 20.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Very high permeability at moderate selectivity targets energy-efficient post-combustion capture membranes; commercial relevance depends on scale-up.
insights.quote: they achieve CO2 permeability of 74,800 Barrer while maintaining a CO2/N2 selectivity of ~20

insights.claim: Polyimide-based versions retain about 85% of initial permeability after six months of ageing at room temperature.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Addresses a typical membrane weakness (physical ageing) but only six months at room temperature is shown.

insights.claim: Conventional mixed-matrix membranes cannot fully use the porous filler's intrinsic transport because high filler loadings cause aggregation and non-ideal interfacial effects.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Identifies the engineering bottleneck for MMMs in carbon capture.

insights.claim: A weak-interaction inlaying strategy that overturns the reliance on strong polymer-filler interactions balances polymer-filler and filler-filler interaction energies, enabling COF loadings up to 75.5 vol% with uniform dispersion and good interfacial compatibility.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A different design principle for high-loading membranes, potentially applicable to other fillers.
insights.quote: enables high COF loadings of up to 75.5

insights.claim: The resulting membranes preserve the intrinsic structure and transport properties of single-crystal COFs, creating filler-dominated pathways for fast CO2 transport.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Mechanism explanation for the high permeability claim.

insights.claim: Energy-efficient carbon capture with membranes requires high gas permeability and selectivity, long-term stability and scalable solution processability.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Criteria checklist for evaluating membrane capture technologies and their commercial readiness.

insights.claim: Authors are at Tianjin University and collaborators including EPFL's Laboratory of Advanced Separations and USC, funded by Chinese national and regional programs.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Indicates Chinese academic leadership in advanced separation materials research.
